newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army trainee who faced rape charges dead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army trainee who faced rape charges dead.

text.p: U.S. Army investigators at the scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground were probing Saturday the death of a trainee facing court martial on charges he raped a female soldier, a base spokesman said.
The death was initially described as a sucicide by base officials, but investigators later said they had not yet made a "characterization" of the incident, base spokesman Ed Starnes told Reuters.
"A soldier discovered his roommate's body in their barracks room," Starnes said. "We don't know if it was a suicide. It's still being investigated."
The soldier, who was not identified pending notification of relatives, was due to face a court martial trial Tuesday on charges he raped a fellow trainee in June, Starnes said.
The soldier had completed his training at the base but had remained there pending his court martial trial.
The case was unrelated to a rape and sexual misconduct scandal focusing on drill instructors and a commander at the proving ground, he said. "It was not tied to the ongoing investigation."
Twenty soldiers have been implicated in that investigation and three face court martial trials starting next month.
